title: New growth_groups catalog block parsed with legacy jint (silent float truncation + i32 wrap), bypassing the jint_strict integer bar its 5.9 sibling enforces
evidence:
b.growth_groups.bias_prob_permille = jint(gobj, "bias_prob_permille", -1)
			b.growth_groups.min_members = jint(gobj, "min_members", -1)
			b.growth_groups.max_members = jint(gobj, "max_members", -1)
			b.growth_groups.radius_tiles = jint(gobj, "radius_tiles", -1)
			b.growth_groups.member_weight_permille = jint(gobj, "member_weight_permille", -1)  — vs jint itself (core/catalog.odin:1128): "case json.Integer: return i32(x)\n\t\tcase json.Float:   return i32(x)" and the sibling directly above (core/catalog.odin:775): "b.cap_fraction_permille, _ = jint_strict(obj, \"cap_fraction_permille\", -1)" with its comment "JINT_STRICT (the new-catalog integer bar, ODN-10): a decimal/wrong-typed fraction is a load rejection, never a silent truncation"; jint_strict's own doc: "an out-of-i32-range integer (|v| > i32::MAX) and ANY other JSON type (string/bool/null) also reject — a huge value must never wrap through the i32 cast (e.g. a cooldown of 2^32+4 silently becoming 4)"
detail: jint silently truncates a JSON float ("bias_prob_permille": 750.9 loads as 750 and passes the 1..999 check) and wraps out-of-i32-range integers through the i32 cast ("radius_tiles": 4294967301 = 2^32+5 loads as 5, passing the > GROWTH_MIN_SEP_TILES check) — the exact wrap class jint_strict was hardened against (regression row "cooldown wraps i32" uses 4294967300). The new growth_groups test rows cover missing/zero/bounds but no decimal or wrap row. Catalog JSON is the system's data boundary and ODN-10's integer-only bar applies.
recommended_fix: Parse all five growth_groups keys with jint_strict (mirroring cap_fraction_permille), fail-fast on ok=false, and add catalog_test rows for a decimal value and a 2^32+N wrap value per key group.
